chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mufazzal ibn Umar said,
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who had a house, and a believer needed to dwell in it, but he prevented him from it,'

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'O My Angels! Is My servant being stingy upon My servant regarding dwelling in the house of the world? By My Honour and My Majesty! He shall not dwell in My Gardens, ever!'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of denying a believer housing?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize the spiritual weight of housing as a fundamental social right, framing the denial of shelter not merely as a financial transaction but as a divine test of generosity. The Imam employs a rhetorical divine declaration, where God contrasts the believer's stinginess over temporary worldly accommodation with the eternal reward of dwelling in Paradise, thereby elevating the act of providing housing to a key determinant of one's ultimate fate.
